# faraday_scope (Resource)



## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "faraday_cohort" "customers" {
  name        = "customers"
  stream_name = "orders"
}

resource "faraday_scope" "export" {
  name    = "export"
  preview = true
  population = {
    cohort_ids = [faraday_cohort.customers.id]
  }
  payload = {}
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Human-readable label for this scope. Each scope must have a unique name.
- `payload` (Attributes) The data to include for each person in this scope. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--payload))
- `population` (Attributes) The people to include in a scope. Leave `cohort_ids` empty to include the entire US population. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--population))
- `preview` (Boolean) A preview scope provides only a limited number of output records, but it is not billed.

### Read-Only

- `archived_at` (String) If not null, this resource will no longer receive updates, but will still be visable.
- `columns` (Attributes) Metadata about the columns in this scope. Useful for advanced target configuration. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--columns))
- `created_at` (String) When this resource was created.
- `id` (String) A unique ID for this resource.
- `last_read_input_at` (String) The last time this resource's input was read.
- `last_updated_config_at` (String) The last time this resource's configuration was updated. If this is more recent than last_updated_output_at, the resource will be rebuilt.
- `last_updated_output_at` (String) The last time this resource successfully built.
- `population_count` (Number) Count of the population. If a person appears in multiple cohorts, they are only counted once.
- `population_residence_count` (Number) Residence count of the population. If a residence appears in multiple cohorts, it is only counted once.
- `resource_type` (String) The type of this resource.
- `status` (String) The current state of this resource and any updates.
- `status_changed_at` (String) When the status of this resource was last updated.
- `status_error` (String) If this resource has `status == "error"`, this will contain an error message.
- `updated_at` (String) When this resource was last updated.

<a id="nestedatt--payload"></a>
### Nested Schema for `payload`

Optional:

- `attributes` (List of String) Include additional traits. For traits created through `output_to_traits` via `/datasets`, specify the trait name. For traits from Faraday's Internal Graph (FIG), specify the name prefixed by `fig/` ex. `fig/age`.
- `cohort_ids` (List of String) Specify a list of cohort membership(s) to include. The list can include any cohort, not just those in `population.cohort_ids`.
- `explainability` (Boolean) Opt-in to include prediction explainability.
- `location` (Attributes) Include each person's proximity to the locations of one or more atlases. Distances are measured to the nearest edge of a location's geometry and published in the unit set by `distance_output_units`. The distance bounds in `conditions` are always in meters. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--payload--location))
- `max_attribute_observation_date` (String) The maximum date for FIG attribute observations used in the scope payload. When set, only attribute data observed on or before this date will be included. If not set, the freshest available data is used.
- `outcome_ids` (List of String) Include the propensity score(s) from the specified outcome(s).
- `persona_set_ids` (List of String) Include the persona assignment(s) from the specified persona set(s). Personas are assigned to everyone in the population matched at the individual or address level, including address-level people who were not used to build the persona set.
- `recommender_ids` (List of String) Include the recommendation(s) from the specified recommender(s). This feature is experimental and subject to change. To enable this feature, contact your account manager.

<a id="nestedatt--payload--location"></a>
### Nested Schema for `payload.location`

Optional:

- `conditions` (Attributes) Which atlas locations each person is matched against, and the distance bounds for a match. If absent, each person is matched against every location in the account's atlases at any distance. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--payload--location--conditions))
- `distance_output_units` (String) The unit `fdy_location_distance` is published in. Defaults to `meters`. `max_distance` and `min_distance` are always given in meters, whatever this is set to. Changing the unit on a scope that already feeds a target changes that column's values on the target's next build.
- `select` (String) Whether to include only the nearest matching location for each person, or every matching location. `all` requires `max_distance`. The choice sets the shape of the three location columns in the scope payload — `fdy_location_name`, `fdy_location_reference_key` and `fdy_location_distance`. Under `nearest` each column holds a single scalar describing that one location. Under `all` each column holds a JSON array ordered nearest first, and the three arrays are index-aligned: the i-th element of each describes the same location. `fdy_location_distance` is therefore a number under `nearest` and text under `all`, so any target already receiving these columns must be rebuilt after the choice changes. A person matching no location has no location data: all three columns are empty under either choice, rather than holding an empty array.

<a id="nestedatt--payload--location--conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `payload.location.conditions`

Optional:

- `atlas_ids` (List of String) The atlases whose locations each person is matched against. If this is empty or absent, every atlas in the account is used.
- `location_reference_keys` (List of String) Match each person only against the locations carrying these reference keys. A reference key is unique only within one atlas, so these keys are matched in every atlas each person is matched against. Select a single atlas to restrict them to that atlas' keys.
- `max_distance` (Number) A person only matches a location if they are no further than this many meters from it.
- `min_distance` (Number) A person only matches a location if they are at least this many meters from it.
- `property_conditions` (Attributes List) Match each person only against the locations whose properties satisfy these conditions. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--payload--location--conditions--property_conditions))

<a id="nestedatt--payload--location--conditions--property_conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `payload.location.conditions.property_conditions`

Required:

- `property` (String) The name of the location property, as defined by its atlas' `output_to_locations`, or `name` or `reference_key` to filter on the location's own name or reference key.

Optional:

- `_eq` (String) Equal to
- `_gt` (Number) Greater than
- `_gte` (Number) Greater than or equal to
- `_in` (List of String) Value is one of
- `_lt` (Number) Less than
- `_lte` (Number) Less than or equal to
- `_matches` (String) Value contains a match to the regex (re2) expression provided. For an exact regex match, use the ^ and $ characters as specified by the (re2 documentation)[https://github.com/google/re2/wiki/Syntax].
- `_neq` (String) Not equal to
- `_nin` (List of String) Value is not one of
- `_nnull` (Boolean) Value is not null
- `_null` (Boolean) Value is null (nulls are otherwise excluded)
- `optional` (Boolean) Optional property conditions are unioned together, when combined they select locations that meet either property condition. At least one optional condition must be satisfied.





<a id="nestedatt--population"></a>
### Nested Schema for `population`

Required:

- `cohort_ids` (List of String) Include people from the specified cohorts in this scope.

Optional:

- `exclusion_address_level_cohort_ids` (List of String) Exclude every individual who shares an address with any individual in the specified cohorts.
- `exclusion_cohort_ids` (List of String) Exclude people from the specified cohorts in this scope.


<a id="nestedatt--columns"></a>
### Nested Schema for `columns`

Read-Only:

- `columns_for_mode` (Attributes) Available columns for different modes of target export. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--columns--columns_for_mode))
- `identity_columns` (List of String) First party identifiers from all dataset `identity_sets` populating this scope.
- `payload_columns` (Attributes List) Payload columns. The shape is a 1:1 mapping of machine-readable payload column names to human-readable column names. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--columns--payload_columns))

<a id="nestedatt--columns--columns_for_mode"></a>
### Nested Schema for `columns.columns_for_mode`

Read-Only:

- `aggregated` (Attributes List) Available columns for a given mode of target export. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--columns--columns_for_mode--aggregated))
- `hashed` (Attributes List) Available columns for a given mode of target export. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--columns--columns_for_mode--hashed))
- `identified` (Attributes List) Available columns for a given mode of target export. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--columns--columns_for_mode--identified))
- `referenced` (Attributes List) Available columns for a given mode of target export. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--columns--columns_for_mode--referenced))

<a id="nestedatt--columns--columns_for_mode--aggregated"></a>
### Nested Schema for `columns.columns_for_mode.aggregated`

Read-Only:

- `aggregation` (String) The method of aggregation. Applies to aggregation targets only.
- `aggregation_criteria` (String) For scope columns that can be aggregated with `countif` (currently just persona sets), this is the value being counted (i.e. the persona ID). Applies to aggregation targets only.
- `is_identity_col` (Boolean) Set this to true when exporting first party identifiers (given by <a href="https://faraday.ai/developers/reference/createdataset">identity_sets</a>). If `true`, `scope_col` represents the dataset field name being selected (ex: "client_email").
- `output_col` (String) The name of this column in the target export. Can be the same as `scope_col`.
- `scope_col` (String) The name of the scope column to export. Users can supply either the machine-readable name (with underscored uuid) or the human-readable name (with literates).
